source.title: Single-Bit-per-Weight Deep Convolutional Neural Networks without Batch-Normalization Layers for Embedded Systems
source.authors: Mark D. McDonnell; Hesham Mostafa; Run-Chun Wang; A. Schaik

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains image classifiers with and without batch-normalization and measures test error across datasets, model widths, and weight precisions. This is a conceptual test of conditions affecting natural-label generalization, but it does not test any listed version directly.
record.gate_note: The study reports test errors for its own BN and activation variants. It does not report training error, so these results do not establish a train-test gap. The BN-related findings are outside the named versions and are recorded with versions ["none"]. Cited findings from other work are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures BN-removal and activation variants, not any listed claim version. It cites original generalization studies, including the large-batch finding, but supplies no corresponding experiment. Its width comparisons lack training-error measurements establishing that widening occurs beyond interpolation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that removing BN generally incurs a potentially small, setting-dependent accuracy penalty; retaining final BN often reduces it, and learning BN scales and shifts is not consistently beneficial. They recommend considering sReLU where hardware costs matter. Qualify the ImageNet conclusion: those experiments retain final BN and do not test complete BN removal.
record.recipe_differences: Uses backpropagation and stochastic gradient descent with momentum and weight decay; compares BN and shifted-ReLU variants, rather than testing the listed claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported test-error differences vary by dataset, network width, weight bit-depth, and ImageNet test mode (centre crop or multi crop).

fits_no_version.finding: BN-removal costs depend on dataset, width, precision and evaluation mode. On CIFAR-10, all-sReLU error exceeds the best variant by 0.09–0.19 percentage points with binary weights and 0.87–1.07 points with full precision. On ImageNet, retaining only final BN costs about 0.3 points for width 2.5 with centre cropping, but substantially more for width 1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Replacing internal BN–ReLU combinations with sReLU can preserve much of image-classification accuracy under suitable architectures and training adjustments; retaining final BN can reduce the penalty.

record.peer_reviewed: Asia-Pacific Conference on Intelligent Robot Systems
record.problems: Training errors are not reported, so train-test gaps cannot be assessed from these tables. CIFAR width-10 and ImageNet entries are single runs; the paper gives spread over 10 repeats only for width-4 CIFAR plots. ImageNet comparisons include only Baseline 1 and final-BN-only variants.
record.rows_left_out: None; all reported table entries for CIFAR 10, CIFAR 100, and ImageNet are included.

untested.parts: No random-label fitting or held-out random-label comparison.
No established zero-training-error threshold or post-interpolation width sweep; experiments use weight decay and augmentation.
No fully connected comparator or local-connectivity intervention.
Batch size is fixed at 125; no large-versus-small batch comparison or batch-dependent recipe adaptation.
No dropout intervention; BN removal does not test dropout removal.
No magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap ranking, or comparison with norm and margin measures.
No memorization-based example selection, removal, or retraining comparison.

record.verdict_notes: All 56 extracted error values match the supplied tables. These are the study's method-performance comparisons and should not serve as evidence for V1–V8. Missing training error specifically prevents establishing V2's post-interpolation condition; held-out error itself is measurable. ELU and mean-only-BN results omitted from rows also fit no listed version. Table III's printed gap column contains arithmetic inconsistencies, but the extracted baseline and final-BN values are transcribed correctly.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of natural-label and random-label generalization.
No width sweep around the zero-training-error threshold or test-error peak.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers and SGD.
No sharpness or other generalization-measure comparison.
No removal of memorized training examples.
